generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: DOORDASH TO BUY INSTACART FOR $17 BILLION, UNITING 2 DELIVERY GIANTS
Summary: DoorDash will acquire Instacart for $17 billion. Instacart shareholders will receive $65 per share, 26% over the company's price on October 22. Combining the companies' technology and infrastructure will result in faster deliveries and more affordable prices. The deal is expected to close late next year or in 2028.

Editorial idea:
A major delivery-market consolidation brings two large platforms under one roof, promising operational scale while reducing the number of independent choices for customers and workers.

Central subject:
The proposed $17 billion DoorDash acquisition of Instacart

Visual relationship:
Two distinct delivery routes converge into one shared distribution path, conveying the merger's combination of technology and infrastructure and the tension between efficiency and concentration.

Composition:
A grounded overhead view of two separate neighborhood delivery routes with distinct starting areas gradually joining at a central transfer point, then continuing as one broader route toward several homes and storefronts. Keep the joining point and the unequal scale of the two routes visually clear.

Permitted literal elements:
Two separate delivery routes
Neighborhood storefronts and homes
A central convergence point
One combined route after the convergence
Small delivery parcels as route endpoints

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Logos
Rendered text
Unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Do not depict the acquisition as completed if it is only proposed
Do not imply guaranteed faster deliveries or lower prices beyond the stated deal rationale
Do not make one company visually disappear before the routes converge
Do not use generic delivery imagery without showing the combination of two systems

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
